raw.product_description: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with a three-layered architecture. The Observe Layer uses lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns (application usage, activity sequences, time allocation). The Intelligence Layer (Brain) detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift" in workflows. The Execution Layer (Agent Factory) automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities with built-in approval gates. It leverages existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify AI automation opportunities.

core_insight.if_wrong: If AI-first companies cannot precisely identify and quantify work patterns, or if the system cannot accurately interpret intent and drift, then the AI automation generated will not be high-ROI or scalable.

core_insight.why_different: narma focuses on observing the 'Work Graph' and leveraging existing foundation models, rather than building proprietary LLMs, to automate work processes and provide continuous AI lift.

raw.thesis: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies, designed to observe, analyze, and automate work processes using AI. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: "Observe" uses desktop sensors to capture work patterns, the "Intelligence Layer" interprets employee intent and business value from these patterns, and the "Execution Layer" (Agent Factory) automatically generates and deploys AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. This system aims to provide "Continuous AI lift" by continuously identifying and automating tasks, focusing on the "Work Graph" rather than building proprietary LLMs. It addresses the challenge of AI-first companies struggling with quantifying AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and operational drift. The venture targets AI-first enterprises that want to scale AI automation. The founder's goal appears to be a growth startup, given the focus on enterprise AI automation and continuous improvement. The venture is at the idea stage, with the description outlining a conceptual architecture and vision rather than a built product.
